Summarise the supplied source text in at most 100 words. Be concise and objective.
Report only information supported by the source. Attribute claims, opinions, and

summary: Chief Puraka’s Apurinã community in southern Amazonas has reintroduced agroforestry, producing food and selling surplus. OPAN’s Magno de Lima dos Santos says it has improved dietary diversity and revived cultural practices. The community faces threats from land grabbing, deforestation and advancing agriculture; Puraka fears outsiders could take its territory. Other Indigenous groups report similar threats. OPAN supports forest-based livelihoods, including managed fishing and Brazil nut harvesting. Greenpeace spokesperson Cristiane Mazzetti says protecting forests and territorial rights is essential for these activities to generate income and opportunities.
